summary: This bill creates a federal crime with up to 2 years in prison (or 5-20 years if serious injury results, or 10 years to life if death results) for intentionally fleeing a Border Patrol agent or assisting officer by motor vehicle within 100 miles of the U.S. border, and makes noncitizens convicted of it inadmissible, deportable, and ineligible for asylum or other immigration relief.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It focuses solely on criminal penalties and immigration consequences.
No tax-related provisions appear in the bill text.

The bill directly amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to add convictions for evading Border Patrol as grounds for inadmissibility, deportability, and ineligibility for relief including asylum. It strengthens border enforcement mechanisms and restricts immigration benefits for those convicted, aligning strongly with restricting immigration and enforcing borders.

The core of the bill creates a new federal criminal offense for evading Border Patrol near the border with escalating penalties (up to life imprisonment if death results). This expands criminal liability and imposes stricter sentencing for specific evasion conduct, pushing toward tougher sentencing and policing.
